correctness.rationale: The full feasible polytope can be verified directly. Adding the two proportionality surpluses gives (b−a)(d−c)≥0, so put h=d−c≥0. The separate constraints are y h≤f−e≤x h, where x=1−2a>y=1−2b>0. Thus p decomposes as 2c S + 2e Q plus a nonnegative residual supported on D,F with F/D ratio in [y,x]; the residual splits between H1 and H2 (and vanishes if h=0). This proves the four-vertex hull and supplies the corrected intermediate identity for the imprecise adding/subtracting sentence in RESULT.md line 22; it does not change the Finding. Direct variance evaluation gives Φ(Q)>Φ(S), Φ(H1)>Φ(H2)=Φ(R), and 4(Φ(R)−Φ(S))=g_x(y). The law of total variance adds a strictly positive between-mean term for any nontrivial mixture of the two tied candidates, whose first mean utilities differ. End signs g_x(0)<0<g_x(x) and strict concavity give one interior crossing. The two one-good-each allocations are EFX; in F, agent 1 has utility zero, fails EF1 and falls below its positive MMS. The exact witness values are 17/100 and 13/80 with t=5/6. These arguments apply on the stated open chamber, not its boundary. The frozen verifier and recorded 330 finite exact-rational checks were inspected, not executed; the universal conclusion is analytic.

value.rationale: The minimal setting in which the proposed fairness objective was known to fail lacked a boundary identifying when the objective actually loses ex-post fairness. The classification determines both sides and distinguishes coexistence of two optima from an optimal interpolation at equality. This is a motivated exact gap in understanding the objective, not a new numerical witness or a claim for larger allocation problems.
